title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: a cycle ξ on a smooth quasi-projective X is called 'Albanese-equivalent to 0' (def. 1.1) if ξ = Z(𝔑) := pr_{X*}(Z·(X×𝔑)). Here T is a smooth parameter variety, Z is a cycle on X×T, and 𝔑 is a 0-cycle on T of degree 0 whose Albanese sum S_T(𝔑) ∈ Alb(T) vanishes. The set N(X) (later N'(X)) of such cycles is to be shown to be a graded ideal of A*(X). It should be stable under f^* and f_*, contain cycles rationally equivalent to 0, and be contained in algebraic equivalence. The quotient A'*(X) is then a ring.

This page proves closure under addition. Take z = Z(𝔑) with data (T, Z, 𝔑) and z' = Z'(𝔑') with data (T', Z', 𝔑').
- Put T_1 = T×T'. Pull Z and Z' back to Z_1 and Z'_1 on X×T×T' (see the margin diagram X×T ← X×T×T' over T ← T×T').
- Lift the parameters along sections: 𝔑_1 = 𝔑×a' and 𝔑'_1 = a×𝔑', for chosen points a ∈ T, a' ∈ T'.
- By functoriality of the Albanese map under the sections t↦(t,a') and t'↦(a,t'), S_{T×T'}(𝔑×a') = S_T(𝔑) = 0 and similarly for 𝔑'_1. The margin note 'Lemme à dégager' asks for this to be isolated as a lemma. Both lifts have degree 0.
- By the projection formula, Z_1(𝔑_1) = Z(pr_*(𝔑×a')) = Z(𝔑) = z, and likewise Z'_1(𝔑'_1) = z'.
- The cross terms vanish: Z_1(a×𝔑') = Z(pr_{1*}(a×𝔑')) = Z(deg(𝔑')·a) = 0. This needs a chosen so that Z(a) is defined; similarly Z'_1(𝔑_1) = 0 for a suitable a'.
- Hence with Z_2 = Z_1+Z'_1 and 𝔑_2 = 𝔑_1+𝔑'_1 (still degree 0, Albanese sum 0) one gets Z_2(𝔑_2) = z+z'.

So N(X) is a subgroup. The next page adds gradedness and the inclusion of linear equivalence: on P^1 every degree-0 0-cycle has S = 0. It then starts on f^*-stability.

In modern terms the equivalence is the subgroup of CH^i(X) generated by Γ_*(ker alb_T) over all smooth T and correspondences Γ. This is exactly the second step F^2 of the filtration later introduced by H. Saito (1979), and the 'Albanese kernel' step of Bloch–Beilinson/Murre-type filtrations. The ring A'*(X) is the corresponding quotient.
errors: The previous page announces a proof for ξ·ξ', but what is proved here is closure under the sum ξ+ξ'. The product (ideal property) needs a separate, easy argument: Z(𝔑)·w = (Z·pr^*w)(𝔑).

Gaps are acknowledged but not filled. Defined intersections need a moving argument: choosing a, a' so that Z(a) and Z'(a') are defined, and making Z_1·(X×𝔑_1) proper. The functoriality S_{T×T'}(𝔑×a') = S_T(𝔑) is left as a 'lemme à dégager'.
The degree-0 condition on 𝔑 is used essentially (for the cross terms to vanish) and was only added as an insertion, so it must be part of definition 1.1.
The conclusion should read 'sous-groupe de Cyc(X)' or '...de A(X)', not 'de X'.

ideas.what: Define an adequate-type equivalence on cycles: z ~ 0 iff z = Z_*(𝔑) for a correspondence Z from a smooth T and a degree-0 0-cycle 𝔑 on T with trivial Albanese sum. Show it gives a graded ideal stable under f^*, f_*, between rational and algebraic equivalence, with quotient ring A'*(X).
ideas.modern_name: Albanese equivalence; second step F^2 of the Saito filtration (Γ_*(ker alb_T)); Bloch–Beilinson / Murre F^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Saito (1979, 'Abelian varieties attached to cycles of intermediate dimension'); related ideas by Bloch, Beilinson, Murre, Jannsen in the 1980s–90s
ideas.where_published: Not in the published texts I know of (not in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles', 1969)

ideas.what: Closure under addition by passing to the product parameter space T×T' and lifting 0-cycles along sections 𝔑×a', a×𝔑'.
ideas.modern_name: Standard product-of-parameter-spaces trick for equivalences defined by families

ideas.what: Functoriality of the Albanese sum along sections: S_{T×T'}(𝔑×a') = S_T(𝔑).

missed.claim: Grothendieck (between 1965 and about 1971) defines 'Albanese equivalence' as cycles of the form Z(𝔑) with 𝔑 in the Albanese kernel of a smooth parameter variety. He develops it as an adequate-type relation: a subgroup containing linear equivalence, f^*/f_*-stable, inside algebraic equivalence, giving a quotient ring A'*(X). This is precisely the Saito F^2 step of the conjectural Bloch–Beilinson filtration, usually dated to H. Saito 1979 and later work.
missed.quote: Donc N(X) est bien un sous-groupe de X.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It pushes back the origin of the second step of the motivic/Bloch–Beilinson filtration on Chow groups into Grothendieck's work on the standard conjectures. It suggests he considered a finer 'Albanese' quotient ring A'* alongside algebraic and numerical equivalence.

deep.surprise_reason: The proof on this page is routine bookkeeping. The interest lies in the underlying definition, which anticipates Saito's F^2 filtration by most of a decade. Similar notions were in the air (Samuel, Weil), so a specialist would find this a notable historical detail rather than a shock.
transcription_corrections: 'sous réserve que Z a pu être choisi tel que Z(a) soit défini' is more likely 'sous réserve que a ait pu être choisi tel que Z(a) soit défini'.
'Cas où de même' is probably 'Car de même' or 'On a de même'.
'on prend les remontés' is probably 'en prenant les 0-cycles' or 'par les remontés'; uncertain.
The final line 'sous-groupe de X' is likely shorthand for a subgroup of the cycle group of X.
